title: Teresa Teng's birth chart
metaDescription: Teresa Teng's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.0° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the nine placements whose signs are settled, fixed leads with four. Fixed weight is the scheme’s deep keel: slow to turn, near-impossible to capsize.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 9.0° Aquarius. That falls in the first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the classical scheme — an air sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 5.6° Aquarius, Venus was at 25.9° Pisces, Mars was at 22.5° Pisces. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Neptune and Pluto: 1.5° from an exact sextile. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, the Sun square Jupiter at 3.0°, and the Sun conjunction Mercury at 3.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 9.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Pisces at 25.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Libra at 27.3° is in exaltation. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 air, 3 water, 1 earth, 1 fire by element and 4 fixed, 3 cardinal, 2 mutable by mode. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.0° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
